source.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
source.authors: Yipeng Zhao; Qi-Shun Yang; Shenzhe Zhu; Shu Yang; Di Wang

page_placements.theme: Reasoning modes and supplied reasoning alter vulnerability

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of supervised fine-tuning on an aligned chat model using benign data and measures harmful-request fulfillment, matching the intervention and behavioral measure in the fine-tuning safety claim. The reasoning corpus, models, and training setup are new settings.
record.gate_note: Rows focus on HEx-PHI harmfulness rates after benign reasoning SFT and reported safety-rate changes under SDP. The study does not measure per-token KL, prefilling or other opening-token bypasses, or whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety. SafetyBench accuracy and representation diagnostics are not harmful-compliance rates; probe results are recorded under fits_no_version. The cited results from other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned instruct models on benign reasoning data (AM-DeepSeek, MetaMathQA) with no harmful content. It reports HEx-PHI harmful-fulfillment rates before and after, which bears directly on V2 in a new setting (reasoning SFT, GPT-4o-mini judge). It uses the same benchmark as Qi et al. (2310.03693) but a different corpus and judge, so T3 rather than T1. Its other main contribution, the SDP mitigation, is the study's own method and does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add three points the authors stress. RIM is a decision failure, not a perception failure: harm is still recognised but not acted on. Degradation runs mainly through extended-thinking responses. The authors frame RIM as conditional, emerging only in Qwen2.5 3B/7B among the settings they evaluated.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign reasoning SFT, LoRA, and harmful-request evaluation on aligned instruct models; the study does not specify enough of the original recipe here to establish an exact match. Its training corpus is reasoning-focused and the main intervention uses 10,000 examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model family and scale, training corpus, SDP penalty weight and layer scope, and whether responses use extended thinking. The paper reports HEx-PHI judge re-evaluation variability of 0.35 to 0.52 pp standard deviation across six judgings for three configurations, with a maximum range of 1.3 pp.

fits_no_version.finding: After AM-SFT, harm-perception probes stay near-perfect while safety-decision probes collapse to the majority-class baseline in 3B and 7B. 14B decision encoding is not disrupted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign reasoning SFT can leave harm recognition intact while degrading the encoded refuse/fulfill decision; probe accuracy is not a compliance rate.

fits_no_version.finding: In AM-SFT models, harmful outputs concentrate in responses that use extended thinking: 41.7% vs 1.9% (3B) and 39.2% vs 4.2% (7B). The 14B model almost never enters <think> and shows no degradation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign reasoning SFT raises harmful compliance mainly through responses in which the learned extended-thinking mode activates.

fits_no_version.finding: The SDP penalty on displacement along a refusal direction in selected layers restores base-level HEx-PHI rates in Qwen 3B and 7B. Outcomes depend on layer scope and penalty weight.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-direction penalties during benign fine-tuning can prevent fine-tuning-induced safety loss (a mitigation claim, not token-depth deepening).

record.code_released: will be released upon publication; no URL stated
record.problems: The positive RIM and SDP results focus on Qwen2.5-Instruct 3B and 7B; the authors characterize cross-dataset, cross-architecture, and 14B results as scope checks, and note the Ministral comparison is not architecture-only matched. HEx-PHI uses one GPT-4o-mini judgment per prompt in the main evaluation, although the paper reports repeat-judging checks. SDP’s safety direction uses a fixed refusal template, and the authors describe their geometric interpretation as a local account rather than a general causal characterization.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable HEx-PHI harmfulness results were left out. SafetyBench accuracy and reasoning-benchmark values were not included as rows because they do not measure harmful-request compliance. CKA ratios, direction cosine similarities, and displacement profiles were not included because they do not measure the versions’ named outcomes. Repeated versions of the same reported SDP result across main text and appendices were not duplicated.

untested.parts: Only reasoning-trace corpora were tested, with 10k to 24k examples. Not tested: few-shot or few-hundred-example benign fine-tuning, ordinary instruction data such as Alpaca or Dolly, and full-parameter fine-tuning (LoRA only).
No per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding-change attacks.
Layer-level CKA, probes and penalty scopes only. No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
No analysis of why safety is concentrated in early response tokens.
SDP constrains hidden-state displacement along a refusal direction; it is not token-depth safety training.

missing.what: Think-inclusive HEx-PHI results (full output judged). The paper says both strip-think and think-inclusive results are reported, but only strip-think numbers appear in the tables.

record.verdict_notes: r8–r17 were relinked to none: they evaluate the authors' own mitigation, and the limits_scope label built on them is dropped. States for r5–r7 were changed to absent, since the authors say these settings 'do not worsen' and judge noise is up to 1.3 pp. The Gemma and Ministral runs use 24,337 examples with model-specific settings, so cross-family contrasts are descriptive. Rates use a single GPT-4o-mini judgment per prompt; the authors report a re-judging SD of 0.35–0.52 pp. This study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests benign reasoning SFT, chiefly with 10,000 examples; does not test fine-tuning with only a few to a few hundred examples or ordinary non-reasoning benign instruction data.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL analysis across response positions.
No tests of compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
The study localizes probe and representation effects to layers and applies a layer-scoped penalty, but does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test why safety differences are concentrated in early response tokens; its reasoning-data mechanism concerns representation displacement, not response-token depth.
SDP is evaluated as a mitigation for reasoning-induced misalignment, not as training that spreads safety across response positions.
